_comment: Occupations: the work people do. They belong to the society, not to a government, so they survive reforms. 'appointed_by' lists offices from any government; whoever holds one of them in the current government may appoint and dismiss, at any time and as often as they like, within the hierarchy of appointments: someone appointed must keep the work until the office that appointed them (or one with higher 'authority', see data/governments) releases them, moves them or dismisses them; lower offices can't touch it (but see society.json 'satisfaction.job_loss': people resent being dismissed or moved). If 'volunteer' is true, or the current government has none of those offices, members may take the work up themselves. There is no limit on how many people do the same work; an optional 'seats': n caps it. 'provides' lists amenities the group has while anyone holds the occupation (a Firekeeper means there is a fire). 'also_trains': other skills the work improves, as a share of the main skill's practice. 'office_is_work': true means holding an office is someone's work: an office holder has no occupation (taking an office gives it up), and nobody may give them one. 'needs_tools': the tools the work can't be done without (items.json). Anyone may be appointed (or volunteer) once the research is done, but they can't work until one of these is in their pack or the camp store: they wait, and take one from the store as soon as one appears (work.json 'auto_take_tools'). It also puts the job higher in the hierarchy of work (society.json 'job_rank'). 'max_per_player': how many occupations one person may hold.

Gatherer.description: Collects plants, roots, nuts and berries for the group.

Sustenance Gardener.description: Plants and tends forest gardens: makes places where Gatherers are sure to find berries, roots and herbs (they don't gather it themselves).

Hunter.description: Goes out to hunt with a spear or bow and brings back meat, hides and bone.

Warrior.description: Defends the group and its territory.

Scout.description: Ranges ahead to find game, water, danger and other groups.

Toolmaker.description: Knaps stone and shapes wood into the tribe's tools and weapons: axes, knives, spears, later bows.

Firekeeper.description: Keeps the communal fire burning by feeding it wood. Without a Firekeeper, or without wood, the fire goes out.

Healer.description: Tends wounds and sickness with herbs and care.

Storyteller.description: Keeps the group's stories alive and speaks for it at gatherings: the tribe's orator.

Builder.description: Raises shelters, windbreaks and storage pits.

Fisher.description: Spears, traps and nets fish in rivers and shallows.
